metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-13, deliberately its own verb/tool rather than a sixth value on CUT's 'shape' parameter — a box grater shreds by friction against a grating surface, physically nothing like a knife's slicing motion CUT models (data/entities/grater.json's own notes). Fixed transformedState (not transformedStateFromParameter, unlike CUT/CRUSH) since GRATE only ever produces one shape here — no 'coarse vs. fine' grate distinction is modeled, unlike CRUSH's fineness parameter, a real depth limit named rather than silently implied absent.
metadata.hashBrownsNote: The real reason this verb exists: hash browns and rösti both start from grated (not sliced/diced) potato — a genuinely different piece shape with a different cooking behavior (much more exposed surface area, cooks fast, binds into a cake via its own released starch rather than staying separate pieces). See potato.json's gratedNote for the rinsed-vs-unrinsed technique distinction this schema does not model.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — re-grating already-grated potato is physically continuous, not a discrete duplication risk, same reasoning as CUT's/MASH's identical flag.

verification.description: Potato reduced to fine shreds, no intact slices/pieces remaining

hazards.note: Box grater's shredding surface directly against fingers/knuckles as the piece being grated gets smaller — a real, distinct hazard from a knife's cut risk
